library.description: Definition-based keyed Store state, AtomStore, family, and optics.

blocks.text: English

服务端每个请求、每个测试用例、每个对话窗口，都需要同一套状态的独立副本；放在模块变量里的状态却被所有人共用。`@migaia/store-keyed` 把“状态是什么”（定义）和“值放在哪里”（store）分开：定义写在模块顶层，不保存值；每个 `createAtomStore` 为这些定义各保存一份值。它还能把大对象拆到字段、把列表拆到每一项分别订阅，并按 id 产出定义。它建立在 `@migaia/reactive` 之上，不依赖 React 或 DOM。

items: 请求或测试之间串状态：服务端一个请求的购物车出现在另一个请求里，上一个测试留下的数据弄坏了下一个。根因是状态放在模块级变量里，被所有导入方共用。
改一个字段，整个对象的读取方都重新渲染：资料对象里在线状态一变，只显示名字的组件也重新渲染。根因是订阅的粒度是整个对象。
改一行，整个列表都重新渲染：勾选一条待办，每一行都重新渲染。根因是每一行读的都是同一个数组，而数组每次修改都会被替换。
按 id 保存的状态越来越多：手写的 `Map<chatId, state>` 只增不减，同一个 id 还可能建出两份状态。根因是按 key 缓存需要保证同一性、容量和清理，手写很难都顾到。
测试要替换依赖，只能改被测代码：价格依赖当前时间，想测夜间折扣只能等到晚上或改成注入参数。根因是被测代码直接引用了具体实现。
定义和值分开。 常见做法把状态包进工厂再到处传实例；这里定义放在模块顶层，每个 store 为它保存一份值，对象和数组初值在每个 store 里各复制一份。示例
字段级订阅。 `focusDef` 只在这个字段变化时通知读取方，写入时自动生成替换了该字段的新对象，不用手写不可变更新。示例
列表项级订阅。 `splitDef` 按 key 把列表拆成逐项定义，改一项只通知这一项；读写已经删除的 key 会报错，而不是返回过期数据。示例
按 id 的定义稳定且有上限。 `familyDef` 对同一个 key 永远返回同一个定义，缓存有 `maxSize`，可以显式 `forget`。示例
测试替身不改被测代码。 `store.override()` 只在一个 store 里替换某个定义，撤销后状态原样保留，并检查替换前后写入方式一致。示例

blocks.text: 下面模拟服务端：两个请求用同一份购物车定义，各自创建 store。用 Node 24 直接运行。
输出：
两个请求用的是同一份定义，但各自的 store 保存各自的值；在一个 store 里原地修改初值对象，也不会影响另一个。
下一步：更多用法看 USEGUIDE 的“按场景查找”；列表很长、只想让变化的那一行更新时，看 改一行不让整个列表重新渲染。
下面是常见的手写共享状态。它能跑，但有三个隐患（只用于说明，不必运行）：
用 store-keyed 时，定义不保存值，每个请求或测试用自己的 store；`splitDef` 让每一行只订阅自己那一项；`familyDef` 按 key 产出定义，有容量上限并可以显式删除。
可以把定义想成“变量声明”，把 store 想成“一块内存”：同一个声明在每块内存里各有一份值。

blocks.text: 几个说法：

items: 释放的单位是整个 store。 store 持有它建出的每一个节点，`dispose()` 时按逆序全部释放；只想提前释放某一个，用 `release(definition)`。
定义可以跨 store 共用，节点不能。 同一个定义在两个 store 里是两个独立的节点。
同步初值。 初值和工厂函数不能返回 Promise；异步数据交给 `@migaia/resource`。

blocks.text: 全部签名、边界行为与错误码见 USEGUIDE.md。下面是使用时最需要记住的约束。

1. `get` 登记依赖，`peek` / `preview` 不登记。 React 适配层的快照读取必须用 `peek` 或 `preview`。 2. `set` 只接受可写定义（`atomDef`、`atomDefFactory`、`writableDef` 及其 optics）。对只读派生写入抛 `TypeError`，经过 `override` 间接指向只读定义时也一样。`set` 在一个批次里执行，不会被外层的追踪记成依赖。 3. `override` 必须保持写入方式。 只读定义可以换成任何同值类型的定义；源定义只能换成源定义；可写派生只能换成参数和返回值相同的可写派生。override 链成环抛 `CYCLIC_OVERRIDE`。 4. 对象初值按 store 复制。 复制用 `structuredClone`，值不可克隆（例如含函数）时抛 `INVALID_OPTION`，宿主缺少 `structuredClone` 时抛 `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`。 5. `preview` 不执行未声明安全的工厂。 `atomDefFactory` 的工厂在 `preview` 里会抛 `PREVIEW_UNSAFE`；确认工厂纯、无副作用后改用 `previewSafeAtomDefFactory`。推测出的值在 Runtime 空闲清理（默认微任务）后，若始终没有变成真实节点就丢弃。 6. `dispose()` 的顺序。 先标记为已释放，再取消全部订阅，再按建出的逆序释放节点；单个失败不阻断其余步骤，多个失败合并成 `AggregateError`（`DISPOSAL_FAILED`）。释放后的任何访问抛 `ATOM_STORE_DISPOSED`。 7. 缓存清理和节点释放是两回事。 `splitDef(...).prune(store)`、`familyDef(...).forget()` / `clear()` 只清理定义的缓存，不释放 store 里已建的节点；节点用 `store.release()` 或 `store.dispose()` 释放。`forget` 之后同一个 key 会得到新定义，旧定义的状态与新定义互不相通。 8. family 需要 `WeakRef` 和 `FinalizationRegistry`。 宿主缺少它们时，调用 `familyDef` / `derivedFamilyDef` 就抛 `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`，不会悄悄退化。 9. key 比较用 SameValueZero，和 `Map` / `Set` 一致：`-0` 与 `+0` 是同一个 key，`NaN` 等于自身。 10. 错误身份。 本包产生的错误带 `source === STORE_KEYED_SOURCE`（`store.keyed`）和 `StoreKeyedErrorCode` 里的 `code`；其他包已有身份的错误保持原样。按 `source` / `code` 判断，不要比较 message。
破坏性迁移：十个高级 optics 原语只从 `@migaia/store-keyed/optics` 导出，`assertNotThenable` 只从 `@migaia/store-keyed/atom/definition` 导出，根入口不保留兼容别名。
不适合的场景：整个应用只有一份全局状态、永远不需要多个作用域时，直接用 `runtime.signal()` / `runtime.computed()` 更简单；需要 Provider 和 Hook 时用 `@migaia/store-react`。
English
包的定位、亮点和心智模型见 README。本指南先按场景给出可以直接运行的示例（Node 24），再逐项列出每个 API 的签名、边界行为和抛错条件。

sections.id: 一份定义每个请求或测试各有一份值
sections.heading: 一份定义每个请求或测试各有一份值

blocks.text: 放在模块级变量里的状态，被所有导入它的代码共用。在服务端，一个请求的购物车会出现在另一个请求里；在测试里，上一个用例留下的数据会弄坏下一个。
常见的修法是把状态包进工厂函数，再把实例传给每个需要它的函数，所有调用点都得改；而且如果有人忘了复制对象初值，几份状态仍然共用同一个对象。
这里的定义（`atomDef`、`derivedDef`）只描述状态，不保存值，所以可以放在模块顶层。每个 `createAtomStore` 为这份定义各自保存一份值；对象和数组初值会在每个 store 里各复制一份。
输出：
Ada 的购物车有 2 件，Grace 的有 1 件，两个请求用的是同一份定义。在一个 store 里原地修改初值对象，另一个 store 的初值仍然是空的。
定义是共用的“词汇”，store 才是值存放的地方。请求或测试结束时释放对应的 store，它创建的所有值都会一起释放。

sections.id: 只订阅大对象里的一个字段
sections.heading: 只订阅大对象里的一个字段

blocks.text: 资料对象里有名字、头像和在线状态。只显示名字的组件，在线状态一变它也重新渲染。
订阅整个对象最简单，于是任何字段一变，所有读取方都收到通知；改成把对象拆成几个独立的 store，写入方又得同时更新好几处。
`focusDef(profileDef, 'name')` 是“这个字段”的定义。读取它只订阅这个字段的值；写入它会生成一个替换了该字段的新资料对象。
输出：

blocks.code:
名字更新：Ada Lovelace
资料对象：{"name":"Ada Lovelace","avatar":"a.png","online":false}

blocks.text: 修改在线状态时，名字的订阅者没有收到通知；写入新名字时收到了，资料对象最终包含两处修改。
路径最多三层（`focusDef(def, 'user', 'address', 'city')`）；更深的路径可以组合多个 `focusDef`，或者写一个 `opticDef`。

sections.id: 改一行不让整个列表重新渲染
sections.heading: 改一行不让整个列表重新渲染

blocks.text: 勾选一条待办，整个列表的每一行都重新渲染，因为每一行读的都是同一个数组，而数组每次修改都会被替换。
手写逐行订阅，要按 id 查找，要处理重新排序和删除，还要把修改不可变地写回数组。
`splitDef(todosDef, (todo) => todo.id)` 把数组拆成按 key 的逐项定义。每一行读取 `todos.of(id)`，只在自己那一项变化时收到通知；写入这一项会把新数组写回源定义。
输出：

blocks.code:
第 t2 行重新渲染：{"id":"t2","title":"修登录 bug","done":true}
列表：t1=false, t2=true

blocks.text: 只有 `t2` 这一行重新渲染，源列表里 `t2` 已标记为完成。
key 必须唯一：读取列表时遇到重复 key 会抛错。读写已经从数组里删除的 key 也会抛错，而不是返回过期数据。

sections.id: 每个对话一份状态不用手写-map
sections.heading: 每个对话一份状态不用手写 Map

blocks.text: 每个对话都需要自己的草稿。手写的 `Map<chatId, state>` 只要没人记得删条目就会一直增长，而且同一个 id 查两次可能建出两份不同的状态。
按 key 缓存看起来简单，但它必须对同一个 key 返回同一个对象、要有容量上限，还要在同一个对话被几个独立作用域同时打开时依然正确。
`familyDef(initial)` 返回一个“key → 定义”的函数：同一个 key 永远得到同一个定义，于是每个 store 都为这个对话保存一份自己的值。`maxSize`（默认 4096）限制缓存大小，`forget(key)` 删除一个 key。
输出：

blocks.code:
同一个 id 是同一个定义：true
产品群草稿：明天发版，4 个字
技术群草稿：（技术群 的空草稿）
缓存的对话数：1

blocks.text: 同一个 id 得到同一个定义；产品群保留了它的草稿，技术群从初始草稿开始；`forget` 之后只剩一个对话被缓存。
超过 `maxSize` 后，最久没用的条目改为弱引用：仍被引用的定义（例如已在某个 store 里实例化）用同一个 key 仍能找到。这需要宿主支持 `WeakRef` 和 `FinalizationRegistry`。

sections.id: 测试时替换一个依赖不用改被测代码
sections.heading: 测试时替换一个依赖不用改被测代码

blocks.text: 价格取决于当前时间，想测夜间折扣，要么等到晚上 10 点，要么改写代码让时间可以注入。
把这类依赖都改成手动注入，会让只为测试存在的参数散落在生产代码里；全局替换 `Date` 又会影响无关的测试。
`store.override(definition, replacement)` 只在这个 store 里把对一个定义的读取转到另一个定义。被测代码仍然使用原来的定义，调用返回的函数就能撤销替换。
输出：

blocks.code:
23 点的价格：50
9 点的价格：100

blocks.text: 时间固定为 23 点时价格是 50；撤销后固定为 9 点，价格是 100。
替换必须保持写入方式不变：只读定义可以换成任何同值类型的定义，可写定义只能换成写法相同的定义，否则抛 `TypeError`。

包内源码按依赖方向分成几层，越往下越不知道上层的存在：

blocks.code:
atom/definition.ts   —— 纯定义：判别联合 + 冻结对象构造器，不 import 任何运行时
atom/kind-constants.ts —— AtomKind 常量表
atom/store.ts         —— AtomStore：把定义落到 IRuntime 上，管理实例表/override/preview
atom/def-optics.ts    —— definition 级 optics：selectDef/opticDef/focusDef/splitDef
atom/optics-path.ts   —— optics 与 split 共用的纯函数（路径读写、按 key 拆分的原语）
family/definition.ts  —— definition 级 family：familyDef/derivedFamilyDef（按 key 缓存 token）
errors.ts / error-code.ts / error-text.ts —— 包边界错误的构造器、稳定错误码、诊断文案
reactive/atom.ts       —— "实例式" atom 协议类型，只有类型和跨 Runtime 校验，无实现

blocks.text: 主入口发布 definition/store、定义 optics、family 与错误工具；`assertNotThenable` 仅从 `@migaia/store-keyed/atom/definition` 发布。十个高级纯 optics 原语由 `@migaia/store-keyed/optics` 发布，其映射直接指向原 `atom/optics-path` owner，无 wrapper 或根兼容别名。原有 atom/store、atom/definition、reactive/atom 窄入口保留。

源文件：`src/atom/definition.ts`、`src/atom/kind-constants.ts`。所有构造器返回 `Object.freeze` 过的纯对象，内部用 `Symbol.for('morning-watch.store.atom-definition')` 打标（`Symbol.for` 使用全局注册表，因此同一个包的两份拷贝——比如同一 realm 的应用主包和 devtools 各自打包了一份——仍能互认对方产出的定义；跨 worker/realm 的传输不属于此品牌协议）。

rows: 源定义，只存初值。每个 `AtomStore` 首次实例化时都会对 `init` 跑一次 `cloneInitial`（见 第 9 节），因此同一个 `atomDef({ list: [] })` 在多个 store 下互不共享同一个对象引用。
源定义，用工厂函数代替静态初值；`create()` 在每个 store 首次实例化时调用一次。`previewSafe` 固定为 `false`——`store.preview()` 遇到它会直接抛错，除非改用下面的 `previewSafeAtomDefFactory`。
与 `atomDefFactory` 唯一区别是 `previewSafe: true`。只应包装纯函数、无副作用的 `create`——React 的 speculative preview 可能被放弃，`create()` 却已经真实执行过了。
`<T>(read: IAtomRead<T>, debugLabel?: string, equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean) => IDerivedDefinition<T>`
`read: IAtomRead<T>`；`debugLabel?: string`；`equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean`
只读派生，`read(get)` 里的 `get` 只能读同一个 store 内的其它定义。`equals` 默认走底层 Computed 的默认比较（`Object.is`），传自定义 `equals` 可以避免"值语义相等但引用不同"时的多余下游通知。
`<T, Args, Result>(read, write: IAtomWriter<Args, Result>, debugLabel?, equals?) => IWritableDerivedDefinition<T, Args, Result>`
`read: IAtomRead<T>`；`write: IAtomWriter<Args, Result>`；`debugLabel?: string`；`equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean`
可写派生，`write(get, set, ...args)` 拿到的 `get`/`set` 是同一个 store 上的 `IAtomGet`/`IAtomSet`，因此写逻辑里可以读写其它定义（典型用途：一次 `set` 同时更新两个关联字段）。
类型守卫，检查内部品牌 Symbol；`AtomStore` 的每个入口方法都用它校验参数，非法值抛 `TypeError('[store] not an atom definition')`。
拒绝 thenable 的守卫；`atomDef`/`atomDefFactory` 内部用它校验初值/工厂返回值。`context` 出现在错误消息里标注调用点。命中 thenable（或读取 `.then` 本身抛错）时抛 `TypeError`，`code: 'INVALID_OPTION'`，原异常（如有）保留在 `cause`。

blocks.code:
const AtomKind = {
  primitive: 'primitive',
  primitiveFactory: 'primitive-factory',
  derived: 'derived',
  writableDerived: 'writable-derived'
} as const
type IAtomKind = (typeof AtomKind)[keyof typeof AtomKind]

blocks.text: `AtomKind` 是一个冻结的常量对象，无调用参数；`definition.kind` 恒取这四个字符串字面量之一，可用于 `switch`/分支判断。
四种 `kind` 组成的判别联合：

blocks.code:
type IAtomDefinition<T> =
  | IPrimitiveDefinition<T>
  | IPrimitiveFactoryDefinition<T>
  | IDerivedDefinition<T>
  | IErasedWritableDerived<T> // writable-derived 在读侧被擦除掉具体 Args

blocks.text: 只有 `primitive`、`primitive-factory`、`writable-derived` 三种可以传给 `store.set()`（`IWritableAtomDefinition`）；`derived` 是纯只读，`store.set()` 遇到它必抛 `TypeError`（见 第 7 节）。
`debugLabel` 只用于调试展示（会被底层 Signal/Computed 当作 `debugName`），不参与相等性判断，也不是 key——两个 `debugLabel` 相同的 `atomDef` 依然是两个独立的定义 token。

同步 Atom 禁止 Promise/thenable 初值。守卫覆盖 object 与 function thenable，并通过 utils probe（`@migaia/utils/function` 的 `probeThenable`）只读取一次 `then`；hostile getter 失败同步转换为 Store Keyed tagged `INVALID_OPTION`，原异常保留在 `cause`。Factory 定义在首次 `get`/`peek`/`preview` 执行返回值时应用同一守卫。

rows: 每次调用都产出一个全新、互不干扰的作用域。
每个 `IRuntime` 对应的默认（不是"唯一"）store，用 `WeakMap<IRuntime, IAtomStore>` 缓存；已 `dispose()` 的旧 store 会被丢弃并重新创建一份。专为不经 Provider 的实例式旧 API 准备，让它们在同一个 Runtime 上共享状态；Provider 场景应该用 `createAtomStore` 各建各的。
会在当前 Computed/Effect 的追踪窗口里建立依赖边；在追踪上下文之外调用等价于普通读取，不会报错。若目标定义还没有实例，会先按定义类型建一份（Signal 或 Computed）。
非追踪读，绝不建边。用于"读一次但不想被记成依赖"的场景（React 适配层的 `getSnapshot` 就是典型例子）。

React 并发渲染下的推测性读。若该定义在本 store 已经有真实实例，直接返回该实例当前值（`peek()` 语义）；否则计算一个只在当前 runtime 版本内有效的临时值，不创建持久实例，Runtime idle cleanup 后（默认 microtask）若始终未被提交（即没有变成真实实例）就自动丢弃缓存。`primitive-factory` 必须显式标记 `previewSafe` 才能在这里执行，否则抛错；出现自我依赖的循环会抛 `[store] circular atom preview detected`。

blocks.code:
store.set(countDef, 1)
store.set(countDef, (previous) => previous + 1) // 函数式更新
store.set(writableDerivedDef, ...customArgs) // 走 write(get, set, ...args)

blocks.text: `store.set(definition, ...args)` 内部用 `runtime.batch(() => runtime.untracked(...))` 包裹：批量提交保证一次 `set` 触发的多次下游重算只通知一轮订阅者；`untracked` 保证 `set` 本身不会被外层正在追踪的 Computed/Effect 误记成依赖。

items: 目标解析为 `primitive`/`primitive-factory`：直接写底层 Signal 的 `.value`，支持传值或传 `(previous) => next` 的更新函数。
目标解析为 `derived`（只读）：抛 `TypeError('[store] atom override resolved to a read-only definition')`——正常情况下 TypeScript 类型已经挡住了直接传只读定义，这条路径主要在 override 把一个可写定义路由到只读目标时触发。
目标解析为 `writable-derived`：调用 `write(store.get, store.set, ...args)`，返回值就是 `write` 的返回值。

blocks.text: 一次写多个源定义时用 `store.setMany`：

blocks.code:
store.setMany([
  [countDef, (previous) => previous + 1],
  [nameDef, 'Ada']
])

items: 只接受源定义（`atomDef`、`atomDefFactory`）。任何一项经 override 解析到非源定义时抛 `OVERRIDE_CONTRACT`。
先解析全部条目、按顺序执行全部更新函数，最后才统一写入。所以只要有一项被拒绝，或者某个更新函数抛错，所有定义都保持原值，订阅者也不会收到通知。
同一个定义出现多次时，后一项的更新函数收到前一项算出的值，结果与逐个 `set` 相同。更新函数如果读取其它定义，读到的是这次调用之前的值。
写入在一个批次里完成，订阅者只通知一轮。

blocks.text: `store.sub(def, onChange)` 内部用 reactive 的静态观察者订阅这一个节点，而不是把底层节点直接交给调用方——实例化策略（何时建 Signal/Computed、是否惰性）因此可以自由演进而不破坏订阅者。首次运行只建立依赖、不触发 `onChange`；此后每次依赖变化都会在 `runtime.untracked()` 里调用 `onChange`，`onChange` 内抛出的异常会被捕获并交给 `runtime.reportError(error, { phase: 'subscription-listener' })`，不会中断其它订阅者，也不会让这个订阅失效。返回的 `unsubscribe` 幂等，可以安全多次调用。
三个重载对应三种"写契约必须保持不变"的规则（详细原因见 第 10 节 第 3 条）；违反规则抛 `TypeError('[store] atom override must preserve the original write contract')`。
行为细节：

items: override 是路由变化，不是节点销毁——旧定义、新定义的底层状态都完整保留，切换后旧定义的现有下游会被强制失效（`invalidateResolved`：只断开下游依赖边，不 dispose 节点本身），下一次读取会重新解析到新目标。
同一个定义可以叠加多层 override（后调用的排在栈顶，解析时总是取最后一层）；`override()` 返回的撤销函数只移除自己那一层，不管它当前是不是栈顶。
override/撤销都会清空内部的 `preview` 缓存（`previews.clear()`），保证 `store.preview()` 不会读到覆盖前的陈旧推测值。
解析走的是可能多层的 override 链；出现循环引用会抛 `Error('[store] cyclic atom override')`。
store 已 `dispose()` 后，调用 `override()` 会先在入口抛 `[store] cannot use a disposed atom store`；已经拿到的撤销函数在 store 已 disposed 后调用则直接是无操作（不会抛错）。

rows: 该定义在本 store 内是否已建实例且有活跃订阅者；定义从未被 `get`/`sub` 过时返回 `false`，不会因为查询本身而建实例。
只摘掉这一个定义对应的实例（断开依赖边、dispose 底层节点），不牵连同一 store 里的其它定义；返回是否确实释放了什么。会同时尝试"override 解析后的目标"与"传入的原始定义"两个 key，兼容"实例是在 override 生效前建的"这种情况。
当前已实例化的定义数量，可用作释放行为的可观测断言点。
释放整个作用域，见 第 9 节。幂等，重复调用是无操作。
创建时传入的 runtime，供适配层交叉校验。

等价于 `derivedDef((get) => select(get(source)), undefined, equals)`。`equals` 默认 `Object.is`：源对象其它字段变了但投影值没变（比如新对象但同一个子字段引用），下游不会被通知。

sections.heading: 4.2 opticDef —— 自定义 lens 的可写投影

blocks.text: 写入时会先用 `optic.get` 取出当前 focus 值，和函数式更新（或直接值）算出的新值做 `Object.is` 比较——相等就直接跳过 `set(source, ...)`，不产生一次空写。`source` 必须是"标准可写定义"（`set(update)` 语义），因为 `opticDef` 内部按这个契约调用 `set(source, optic.set(currentSource, nextFocus))`。

sections.heading: 4.3 focusDef —— 按字段路径的内置 lens

blocks.text: 是 `opticDef` 的一个内置特化：读路径用 `Reflect.get` 沿路径逐层取值，写路径沿路径逐层浅拷贝（数组用 `[...value]`、对象用 `{...value}`）再写回，不修改原对象，也不需要手写不可变更新样板代码。类型层最多支持到三层路径；更深的嵌套需要自己组合多个 `focusDef` 或直接写 `opticDef`。
边界行为：

items: 调用时不传任何路径段，抛 `Error('[store] focusDef requires at least one path segment')`。
读到路径中途遇到 `null`/非对象值，抛 `TypeError('[store] focusDef cannot read path segment <key>')`。
写入时路径中途遇到 `null`/非对象值（且后面还有路径要走），抛 `TypeError('[store] focusDef cannot write path segment <key>')`。
写路径对 `__proto__` 这个 key 做了特殊处理，走 `Object.defineProperty` 而不是 `Reflect.set`，避免原型链污染。

sections.heading: 4.4 splitDef —— 数组按 key 拆分

rows: 返回该 key 对应的可写 item 定义；token 用内部 `Map` 缓存，同一个 key 永远拿到同一个对象引用，跨 store 也一样（因为这是 definition 层，不是实例）。读取时按 `keyOf` 在当前源数组里定位下标；找不到抛 `Error('[store] split def item was removed')`。写入同理，找不到抛 `Error('[store] cannot write a removed split def item')`。
一个 `derivedDef`，值是"当前源数组每一项对应的 `of(key)` 定义"组成的冻结数组；用自定义 `equals`（`shallowArrayEquals`：长度相同且逐项 `Object.is`）比较——重排/新增/删除之外的更新不会让这个数组本身触发下游重跑，数组顺序不变时各项 identity 也保持稳定。
等价于 `store.set(source, (previous) => spliceInsert(previous, item, index))`；`index` 默认 `+Infinity`（追加到末尾），越界会被夹到 `[0, length]` 区间。
按 `keyOf` 过滤掉源数组里全部 SameValueZero 匹配元素，返回是否确实删除了。
只清理 `splitDef` 自己的 key → 定义 token 缓存，不释放 `AtomStore` 里已经实例化的对应节点——那部分要么自己 `store.release(itemDef)`，要么整体 `store.dispose()`。返回本次清理掉的 key 数量。

blocks.text: 源数组里出现重复 key（`keyOf` 算出同一个值）会在 `items` 求值时抛 `Error('[store] splitDef keys must be unique')`。

function readOpticPath(value: unknown, path: readonly PropertyKey[], label: string): unknown
function writeOpticPath(
  value: unknown,
  path: readonly PropertyKey[],
  next: unknown,
  label: string

blocks.text: `readOpticPath` 沿 `path` 逐层 `Reflect.get`；中途遇到 `null`/非对象值抛 `TypeError('[store] ${label} cannot read path segment ${key}')`。`writeOpticPath` 沿路径逐层浅拷贝（数组 `[...value]`、对象 `{...value}`）再写回，不修改原对象；中途遇到 `null`/非对象值（且后面还有路径要走）抛 `TypeError('[store] ${label} cannot write path segment ${key}')`；写入路径命中 `__proto__` 时改走 `Object.defineProperty`，避免原型链污染。两者的 `label` 只用于拼接错误消息，标注是哪个调用点（`focusDef` 内部固定传 `'focusDef'`）。
线性查找第一个 `keyOf(item, index)` 与 `key` 满足 SameValueZero 的下标（与 Map/Set 一致，`-0` 与 `+0` 相等，`NaN` 与自身相等）；找不到返回 `-1`，不抛错。

`findKeyIndex` 的严格版本：找不到时抛 `Error('[store] ${label}')`（实现会添加 `[store] ` 前缀，`label` 不要重复包含它）。`splitDef(...).of(key)` 内部用它，`label` 分别传 `'split def item was removed'`（读）和 `'cannot write a removed split def item'`（写）。

blocks.code: function shallowArrayEquals<T>(left: readonly T[], right: readonly T[]): boolean

blocks.text: 长度相同且逐项 `Object.is` 相等才为真；`splitDef(...).items` 的默认 `equals` 就是它。
遍历 `items` 算出每项的 key 并用 `Set` 查重；出现重复 key 抛 `Error('[store] ${label} keys must be unique')`。返回值是 `Object.freeze` 过的只读数组。

blocks.code: function spliceInsert<T>(list: readonly T[], item: T, index: number): readonly T[]

blocks.text: 不可变插入：复制 `list`，把 `index` 夹到 `[0, list.length]` 区间后 `splice` 插入 `item`，返回新的冻结数组。`splitDef(...).insert` 内部调用它。
不可变删除：过滤掉全部 SameValueZero 匹配 `key` 的元素。`removed: false` 时 `next` 直接是入参 `list` 的原始引用（不做无意义拷贝）；`removed: true` 时 `next` 是新的冻结数组。

blocks.code: function replaceAtIndex<T>(list: readonly T[], index: number, value: T): readonly T[]

blocks.text: 不可变按下标替换：复制 `list` 后把 `list[index]` 换成 `value`，返回新的冻结数组，不做下标越界检查（调用方需自行保证 `index` 合法）。

blocks.code:
class KeyedSplitCache<Key, Item> {
  get(key: Key): Item | undefined
  of(key: Key, create: () => Item): Item
  prune(
    isLive: (key: Key) => boolean,
    shouldEvict?: (item: Item) => boolean, // 默认 () => true
    onEvict?: (item: Item) => void
  ): number
  readonly size: number
  keys(): IterableIterator<Key>
  values(): IterableIterator<Item>
  clear(): void
}

blocks.text: `splitDef` 内部用来缓存 `key → item definition` token 的可复用键控缓存。构造无参数（内部是一个空 `Map`）。`of(key, create)`：缓存已有 truthy 值时直接返回；缺失或已有 falsy 值时调用 `create()` 并覆盖存入。`prune(isLive, shouldEvict?, onEvict?)`：对每个当前缓存的 `key`，只有 `isLive(key)` 为 `false` 且 `shouldEvict(item)`（默认恒 `true`）为 `true` 才删除，即 `!isLive(key) && shouldEvict(item)` 才真正淘汰；淘汰前调用 `onEvict?.(item)` 供调用方自行释放该项持有的资源（例如 dispose 一个实例）；返回本次淘汰的条目数。`splitDef(...).prune(store)` 内部就是用 `isLive = (key) => activeKeysInSourceArray.has(key)` 调用它，不传 `shouldEvict`/`onEvict`（definition token 本身不持有需要 dispose 的资源）。
源文件：`src/family/definition.ts`。旧的"实例式" family 缓存的是已经绑死 Runtime 的实例，同一个 key 在不同 Scope 下永远是同一份状态；definition family 把这一层拆开——family 只缓存 token，token 落到哪个 `AtomStore` 才决定它在哪个作用域下有一份独立的值。
`IFamilyKey = string | number | symbol`。

items: `familyDef(initial)` 内部对每个 key 产出 `atomDefFactory(() => initial(key), ...)`——也就是说 family 定义的 `kind` 恒为 `'primitive-factory'` 且 `previewSafe: false`；如果需要在 `store.preview()` 里读 family 成员，要么改用 `derivedFamilyDef`，要么接受它在 preview 路径下会抛错。
`derivedFamilyDef(read)` 对每个 key 产出 `derivedDef(read(key), ...)`，是只读的。

两者都调用即返回缓存命中的 token；`family.size` 是当前强缓存的条目数；`family.forget(key)` 显式打破该 key 的 canonical identity（已经建出来的 `AtomStore` 实例不受影响，但同一个 key 之后再查会拿到一个新 token——调用方必须先停止使用旧 token，否则同一个逻辑 key 会分裂成两份互不相关的状态）；`family.clear()` 清空全部缓存条目。

blocks.text: `options` 校验细节：非对象（`null`/非 `object`）或读取 `maxSize`/`debugLabel` 本身抛错，会被规整为 `RangeError`，`code: 'INVALID_OPTION'`，消息 `[store] family maxSize must be a positive integer`；`debugLabel` 非字符串抛 `RangeError`，消息 `[store] family debugLabel must be a string`；`maxSize` 非正安全整数同样抛 `RangeError`。

强缓存是一个按访问顺序重排的 `Map`（`maxSize` 条），超出上限时淘汰最久未访问的一条——但淘汰只是从强缓存移除，同时会把它登记进一张 `Map<Key, WeakRef<Definition>>`（强键、弱值） 当"canonical"记录：只要这个 token 还被别处强引用着（比如某个 `AtomStore` 已经实例化过它，或者调用方自己存了一个变量），后续同 key 查找会通过 `WeakRef.deref()` 命中同一个 token 并把它重新提升回强缓存；只有当 token 真正被 GC 回收之后，同 key 才会创建一个全新 token。这套机制依赖宿主支持 `WeakRef` 和 `FinalizationRegistry`——缺失时 `familyDef(...)`/`derivedFamilyDef(...)` 调用本身就会直接抛 `Error('[store] family definitions require WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry; enable these capabilities in the host sandbox')`，不会静默降级成"每次都创建新 token"。
`maxSize` 必须是正整数，否则抛 `RangeError('[store] family maxSize must be a positive integer')`。

源文件：`src/errors.ts`、`src/error-code.ts`、`src/error-text.ts`。本包创建的错误带 `source: 'store.keyed'` 与稳定 `code`；Reactive 或其它已有编码错误保留实际 owner。纯 optic 属性访问失败使用 `OPTIC_ACCESS_FAILED`：可扩展原生错误在原对象附码，保留类型、message、stack；frozen/非 Error 主值经 coded fallback 的 cause 可达。任意值品牌守卫读取失败返回 false。按 source/code 处理（而非 message）。

前三者只在返回的运行时类型上不同（`Error`/`RangeError`/`TypeError`），参数形状完全一致：`code`（必填）、`message`（必填）、`options?.cause`（可选，透传进原生 `Error` 构造器的 `{ cause }`）。返回值都经 `attachErrorIdentity`（来自 `@migaia/utils/error`）打上 `source: 'store.keyed'` 与 `code`，不改动 `stack`/`name`。`createStoreKeyedAggregateError` 额外要求 `errors: unknown[]`（必填，成为 `AggregateError.errors`），不接受 `cause` 选项。

import type { IReadableAtom, IWritableAtom } from '@migaia/store-keyed/reactive/atom'

blocks.text: `AtomStore` 内部用一个可遍历的 `Map<definition, instance>` 保存实例，而不是 `WeakMap`——释放时需要遍历它们逐个断开依赖边、`dispose()` 底层节点，`WeakMap` 做不到这件事。生命周期的最小单位是整个 store，不是单个定义：store 强引用它建出的每一个实例，随 `store.dispose()` 一起批量释放；要提前释放某一个，用 `store.release(definition)`。

`atomDef(init)` 的 `init` 若是对象/数组，第一次在某个 store 里实例化时会跑一次 `cloneInitial`：用 `structuredClone`；宿主不支持时抛 `Error('[store] primitive initial values require structuredClone support')`（`code: 'ENV_UNSUPPORTED'`），值本身不可结构化克隆（如包含函数）时抛 `Error('[store] primitive initial value cannot be cloned independently')`（`code: 'INVALID_OPTION'`，原异常在 `cause`）——刻意不做"部分兜底"，避免悄悄改变原型或别名化函数字段。这保证了同一个定义在多个 store 下不会意外共享同一份可变初值容器。

blocks.code: store.dispose()

blocks.text: 1. 立即置 `disposed = true`（此后所有方法入口都会先抛 `[store] cannot use a disposed atom store`），清空 override 表。 2. 依次调用当时全部活跃订阅（`sub()` 返回的 unsubscribe）——单个订阅取消失败不会阻断其它订阅的取消，错误先收集起来。 3. 通过内部 `LifecycleScope` 按建出的逆序释放全部实例节点（后建的派生通常依赖先建的源，逆序释放避免"源先没了、派生 dispose 时读到已释放状态"）——单个节点 dispose 失败同样先收集不中断。 4. 收集到 0 个错误：正常返回；收集到 1 个：原样 `throw`；收集到多个：包成 `AggregateError('[store] atom store disposal failed')` 抛出。
`dispose()` 幂等，重复调用是无操作，不会重复抛错。

items: `store.release(def)`：只摘一个实例。摘除时先尝试当前 override 目标，仅未释放任何实例时才回退到原始定义，因此即便这个定义后来被 override 过，也能正确摘掉在 override 生效前就建好的旧实例。
`store.dispose()`：摘整个作用域。

blocks.text: `splitDef(...).prune(store)`、`familyDef(...).forget/clear` 这类"family/split 自己的 key→token 缓存清理"都不会连带调用 `store.release()`——token 缓存和 store 的实例表是两张独立的表，各自负责各自的生命周期。

sections.heading: 9.4 override 与 preview 的相互影响

blocks.text: `override()`/其撤销函数都会 `previews.clear()`——这保证 `store.preview()` 不会在 override 状态切换的瞬间读到一份对应旧路由的推测值。`preview()` 本身对已有真实实例的定义直接短路成 `peek()`，只有"还没有真实实例"的定义才会走推测计算路径，且该路径产出的值只在当前版本时钟值内复用（由 `@migaia/reactive/extension` 的 `currentRuntimeVersion(runtime)` 读取），Runtime idle cleanup 后（默认 microtask）如果始终没有变成真实实例就会被丢弃——一个长期挂载的 Provider 不会因为一次被放弃的推测渲染而永久持有一份推测对象。

1. `store.get()` 建依赖边，`peek()`/`preview()` 不建。`get()` 在追踪上下文（Computed 的 `read`、Effect 的回调体）里调用才会真正建边；在普通同步代码里调用它和 `peek()` 效果一样，只是语义上更容易被误用成"以为在别处也会自动追踪"。React 适配层的 `getSnapshot`、`useSyncExternalStore` 的快照读必须用 `peek`/`preview`，用 `get` 会把这次读意外记进当前渲染帧之外某个别的 Computed 的依赖集合，产生难以复现的"串边"问题。

2. `store.set()` 只接受 primitive / primitive-factory / writable-derived。对 `derivedDef` 调用 `set()` 会抛 `TypeError`；这不只是 TypeScript 层的约束——即便通过 `override()` 把一个可写定义间接路由到只读定义，运行时同样会在真正执行写入时抛出，不存在"类型检查绕过后运行时也放行"的漏洞。

3. `override()` 必须保持原有写契约，原因是"读侧统一形态"的代价：`AtomStore.get()` 对全部 4 种 `kind` 一视同仁地读，但 `set()` 需要知道目标究竟按哪种写语义处理参数。如果允许 primitive 被 override 成一个自定义 `writable-derived`，`set(def, update)` 传进去的 `update` 参数在两种写语义下含义完全不同（前者是"新值或更新函数"，后者是"传给自定义 `write` 的任意参数列表"），运行时无法安全分辨该按哪套规则处理。只读定义没有这层顾虑——它自己没有公开的写契约，因此可以被路由到任意同值类型的定义。

4. `atomDefFactory` 的 `create()` 默认不允许在 `store.preview()` 里执行。React 的并发渲染可能发起一次推测渲染又整体放弃；如果 `create()` 有副作用（比如打开一个连接、往某个外部注册表写一条记录），一次被放弃的渲染也会让副作用真实发生且无法撤销。需要在 preview 路径执行的工厂必须显式用 `previewSafeAtomDefFactory` 声明，并且自己保证纯、幂等、无外部可观察副作用——这是调用方的承诺，包本身不做运行时验证。

5. `splitDef(...).prune(store)` 只清理 splitDef 自己的 key→token 缓存，不释放 `AtomStore` 里已经实例化的对应节点。这是刻意的职责分离：`splitDef` 只知道"哪些 key 的定义 token 还有意义"，不知道、也不该知道某个 `AtomStore` 有没有实例化过它——真正的实例释放要么调用方显式 `store.release(itemDef)`，要么依赖 `store.dispose()` 整体收尾。长期滚动大量 key（比如聊天消息列表持续增删）而只调用 `prune()` 不管 store 侧，`splitDef` 内部缓存不会泄漏，但对应 `AtomStore` 里的旧实例会一直累积。

6. 释放粒度是"整个 store"，不是"单个定义"。这是 `atom/store.ts` 顶部注释里明确纠正过的一处历史设计——旧版本的注释宣称"定义不再被引用时实例可回收"，但同时又用数组强引用着全部实例，两者自相矛盾，实际什么都回收不了。现在的诚实做法是：store 强引用它建出的一切，`release(def)` 是唯一的"提前释放单个"入口，真正的批量回收只发生在 `store.dispose()`。

7. `familyDef`/`derivedFamilyDef` 需要宿主支持 `WeakRef` 和 `FinalizationRegistry`，缺失时在调用构造函数那一刻就直接抛出说明性错误，而不是静默降级成"每次都创建新 token / 永不回收"——后者会制造一个悄悄变慢或悄悄泄漏内存的包，比显式报错更难排查。少数嵌入式 JS 引擎或裁剪过的小程序沙箱可能缺这两个全局能力，需要确认目标运行环境或引入等价的 polyfill。

8. `readOpticPath`/`writeOpticPath`/`KeyedSplitCache` 等 optics 底层工具函数是公开导出，不是内部私有实现——它们通过 `@migaia/store-keyed/optics` 发布，是 `focusDef`/`splitDef` 的实现基础，也可以被调用方直接复用来手写自定义 optics/split 逻辑（见第 11 节 完整示例）。但它们是纯函数原语，不做 `AtomStore`/依赖追踪相关的任何事——`readOpticPath`/`writeOpticPath` 纯粹是对象路径读写，`KeyedSplitCache` 纯粹是一个键控缓存，都不认识 `IAtomDefinition`。
一个"每个会话（session）一份状态、字段可独立订阅、列表按 key 拆分、测试期可替身"的组合示例：

Q：`store.set(def, value)` 抛 `TypeError: [store] atom override resolved to a read-only definition`。 `def`（或它被 override 之后解析到的目标）是一个 `derivedDef`。只读派生没有写语义；如果是通过 `override()` 间接路由过去的，检查 override 链条上是否有一步把可写定义指向了只读定义。

Q：`store.override(a, b)` 抛 `TypeError: [store] atom override must preserve the original write contract`。 `a`、`b` 的写语义不匹配：primitive/primitive-factory 只能互相替换，writable-derived 只能被同 Args/Result 的 writable-derived 替换。只有"只读定义"这一侧没有这个限制，可以路由到任意同值类型的定义，见 第 10 节 第 3 条的原因说明。
Q：`familyDef(...)` 一调用就抛 `requires WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry`。 目标运行环境缺这两个 ES2021 全局能力（部分裁剪过的小程序/嵌入式 JS 引擎会缺）。需要确认宿主支持情况，或引入功能等价的 polyfill；这个错误不会静默吞掉，说明包作者刻意选择"宁可显式报错，也不要悄悄退化成不清理内存"。

Q：`store.preview(def)` 抛 `Error: [store] atom factory is not marked preview-safe`。 `def` 是用 `atomDefFactory` 建的（`previewSafe: false`），却在 React 的推测渲染路径（`preview()`）里被读取。要么确认这个工厂函数纯、无副作用后改用 `previewSafeAtomDefFactory`，要么避免在 preview 路径读它。

Q：`splitDef(...).of(key)` 抛 `split def item was removed` / `cannot write a removed split def item`。 该 key 已经不在源数组里了（可能被别处 `remove()` 过，或源数组被直接 `store.set()` 替换掉了该项）。读写前用 `todosSplit.items` 或直接查 `store.get(todosSplit.source)` 确认 key 是否还存在；`of(key)` 拿到的 token 本身在 key 消失后依然是同一个对象，但读写会持续失败直到该 key 重新出现在源数组里。

Q：`store.dispose()` 之后再 `store.get(def)`，为什么直接抛错而不是拿到最后一次的值？ `dispose()` 后的 store 处于终结状态，任何读写入口都会先抛 `[store] cannot use a disposed atom store`。这是有意的：一个已释放的作用域不应该被继续静默使用，否则很容易掩盖"忘记开新 store"的调用方 bug。需要新状态就 `createAtomStore(runtime)` 建一个新的。

Q：`familyDef(...).forget(key)` 之后，之前拿到的旧 token 还能用吗？ 能，旧 token 依旧是一个合法的定义，已经用它实例化过的 `AtomStore` 状态不受影响。但 `forget` 之后同一个 key 再查会创建一个新 token，新旧 token 互不相通——如果代码里还有地方持有旧 token 并继续用它读写，会和"新 token 那一份状态"永久分裂成两份。`forget` 之后应该确保调用方统一切换到新的查找结果，不要混用。
Q：如何创建按 key 分组的状态？ 使用 `familyDef`/`derivedFamilyDef` 与 `createAtomStore` 的公开组合。未发布的实例式 family 源码及其测试已删除；仅属于该实现的 `FAMILY_DISPOSED`/`EVICTION_FAILED` 错误码成员也已移除。

中文

Every server request, every test and every chat window needs its own copy of the same state, yet state kept in a module variable is shared by everyone. `@migaia/store-keyed` separates what the state is (the definition) from where its value lives (the store): definitions sit at module level and hold no value, and each `createAtomStore` keeps its own value for them. It can also split a large object down to fields and a list down to items for separate subscriptions, and produce definitions by id. It is built on `@migaia/reactive` and depends on neither React nor the DOM.

items: State leaks between requests or tests: one server request's cart shows up in another, and data left by one test breaks the next. The cause is state in a module-level variable, shared by everything that imports it.

Changing one field re-renders every reader of the object: the online flag in a profile changes, and a component that only shows the name re-renders. The cause is that subscriptions cover the whole object.
Changing one row re-renders the whole list: ticking one todo re-renders every row. The cause is that every row reads the same array, and the array is replaced on every change.

State kept by id keeps growing: a hand-written `Map<chatId, state>` only grows, and the same id can create two different states. The cause is that a cache by key must guarantee identity, a size limit and cleanup, which hand-written code rarely covers.

Replacing a dependency in a test means changing the code under test: a price depends on the current hour, and testing the night discount means waiting until night or adding an injected parameter. The cause is that the code under test references a concrete implementation directly.

Definitions are separate from values. The usual approach wraps state in a factory and passes the instance everywhere; here definitions stay at module level, each store keeps its own value for them, and object or array initial values are copied per store. Example
Field-level subscriptions. `focusDef` notifies readers only when its field changes, and writing it produces a new object with that field replaced, with no hand-written immutable update. Example

Item-level subscriptions. `splitDef` splits a list into per-key definitions, so changing one item notifies only that item; reading or writing a removed key throws instead of returning stale data. Example
Definitions by id are stable and bounded. `familyDef` always returns the same definition for the same key, the cache has a `maxSize`, and `forget` drops a key explicitly. Example

Test doubles without touching the code under test. `store.override()` replaces one definition inside one store, undoing it leaves the state as it was, and it checks that the write contract is unchanged. Example

blocks.text: Every signature, boundary behaviour and error code is in USEGUIDE.en.md. These are the constraints that matter most in use.

1. `get` records a dependency; `peek` / `preview` do not. Snapshot reads in React adapters must use `peek` or `preview`. 2. `set` accepts only writable definitions (`atomDef`, `atomDefFactory`, `writableDef` and their optics). Writing a read-only derived definition throws `TypeError`, also when an `override` routes to one indirectly. `set` runs in one batch and is never recorded as a dependency by an outer tracking context. 3. An `override` must keep the write contract. A read-only definition can be replaced by any definition of the same value type; a source definition only by a source definition; a writable derived definition only by one with the same arguments and result. A cycle in the override chain throws `CYCLIC_OVERRIDE`. 4. Object initial values are copied per store. Copying uses `structuredClone`; a value that cannot be cloned (for example one containing functions) throws `INVALID_OPTION`, and a host without `structuredClone` throws `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`. 5. `preview` never runs factories not declared safe. An `atomDefFactory` factory throws `PREVIEW_UNSAFE` inside `preview`; use `previewSafeAtomDefFactory` once you have made sure the factory is pure and side-effect free. Speculative values are dropped after the Runtime's idle cleanup (a microtask by default) if they never became real nodes. 6. The order of `dispose()`. It marks the store disposed, cancels every subscription, then releases nodes in reverse creation order; one failure never stops the remaining steps, and several failures are combined into an `AggregateError` (`DISPOSAL_FAILED`). Any access after disposal throws `ATOM_STORE_DISPOSED`. 7. Clearing caches is not releasing nodes. `splitDef(...).prune(store)` and `familyDef(...).forget()` / `clear()` only clear definition caches and leave nodes already created in a store alone; release those with `store.release()` or `store.dispose()`. After `forget`, the same key gives a new definition whose state is unrelated to the old one. 8. Families need `WeakRef` and `FinalizationRegistry`. Without them, calling `familyDef` / `derivedFamilyDef` throws `ENV_UNSUPPORTED` instead of degrading silently. 9. Keys are compared with SameValueZero, as in `Map` / `Set`: `-0` and `+0` are the same key, and `NaN` equals itself. 10. Error identity. Errors produced by this module carry `source === STORE_KEYED_SOURCE` (`store.keyed`) and a `code` from `StoreKeyedErrorCode`; errors from other module that already have an identity keep it. Branch on `source` / `code`, never on the message.

Breaking migration: the ten advanced optics primitives are exported only from `@migaia/store-keyed/optics`, and `assertNotThenable` only from `@migaia/store-keyed/atom/definition`; the root entry keeps no compatibility alias.

When not to use it: when the whole application has one global state and never needs several scopes, `runtime.signal()` / `runtime.computed()` are simpler; for Providers and Hooks, use `@migaia/store-react`.

sections.heading: One definition, a separate value per request or test

blocks.text: State kept in a module-level variable is shared by everything that imports it. On a server, one request's cart shows up in another request; in tests, one case's leftovers break the next.

The usual fix is to wrap the state in a factory and thread the instance through every function that needs it, which changes every call site and still leaves object initial values shared by reference if someone forgets to copy them.

Here the definition (`atomDef`, `derivedDef`) only describes the state and holds no value, so it can stay at module level. Each `createAtomStore` gives that definition its own value, and object or array initial values are cloned for every store.
Output:
Ada's cart has 2 items and Grace's has 1, although both requests used the same definitions. Mutating the initial object in one store leaves the other store's initial value empty.
The definition is the shared vocabulary and the store is the place where values live. Dispose a store when its request or test ends to release every value it created.

sections.heading: Subscribe to one field of a large object

blocks.text: A profile object holds the name, the avatar and the online flag. A component that only shows the name re-renders every time the online flag flips.
Subscribing to the whole object is simplest, so every field change notifies every reader; splitting the object into separate stores instead forces every writer to update several places.
`focusDef(profileDef, 'name')` is a definition for one field. Reading it subscribes only to that field's value, and writing it produces a new profile object with that field replaced.
Output:

blocks.code:
name updated: Ada Lovelace
profile: {"name":"Ada Lovelace","avatar":"a.png","online":false}

blocks.text: Changing the online flag does not notify the name subscriber; writing the new name does, and the profile object ends up with both changes.
Paths can be up to three keys deep (`focusDef(def, 'user', 'address', 'city')`); for deeper paths combine several `focusDef`s or write an `opticDef`.

sections.heading: Update one row without re-rendering the whole list

blocks.text: Ticking one todo re-renders every row, because every row reads the same array and the array is replaced on every change.
Hand-written per-row subscriptions need a lookup by id, care when items are reordered or removed, and code that writes the change back into the array immutably.

`splitDef(todosDef, (todo) => todo.id)` turns the array into one definition per key. Each row reads `todos.of(id)` and is notified only when its own item changes; writing the item writes a new array back to the source.
Output:

blocks.code:
row t2 re-renders: {"id":"t2","title":"fix the login bug","done":true}
list: t1=false, t2=true

blocks.text: Only row `t2` re-renders, and the source list now has `t2` marked done.
Keys must be unique: a duplicate key throws when the list is read. Reading or writing a key that has been removed from the array throws instead of returning stale data.

sections.heading: One state per chat id, without a hand-written Map

blocks.text: Every chat needs its own draft. A hand-written `Map<chatId, state>` grows forever unless someone remembers to delete entries, and two lookups for the same id can create two different states.
Caching by key looks trivial, but it has to return the same object for the same key, bound its size, and still work when the same chat is open in several independent scopes.

`familyDef(initial)` returns a function from key to definition: the same key always gives the same definition token, so every store gives that chat its own value. `maxSize` (default 4096) bounds the cache, and `forget(key)` drops one key.
Output:

blocks.code:
same id, same definition: true
product draft: ship tomorrow, 13 characters
engineering draft: (empty draft for engineering)
cached chats: 1

blocks.text: The same id returns the same definition, the product chat keeps its draft, the engineering chat starts from its initial draft, and after `forget` only one chat remains cached.

Beyond `maxSize`, the least recently used entries are held weakly: a definition still referenced (for example instantiated in a store) is still found for the same key. This needs `WeakRef` and `FinalizationRegistry` in the host.

sections.heading: Swap one dependency in a test without touching the code under test

blocks.text: A price depends on the current hour, and testing the night discount means waiting until 22:00 or rewriting the code so the hour can be injected.
Injecting every such dependency by hand spreads test-only parameters through production code, and global mocks of `Date` leak into unrelated tests.

`store.override(definition, replacement)` routes reads of one definition to another inside this store only. The code under test keeps using the same definition tokens, and calling the returned function undoes the override.
Output:

blocks.code:
price at 23:00: 50
price at 09:00: 100

blocks.text: With the hour fixed at 23 the price is 50; after undoing and fixing it at 9 the price is 100.

An override must keep the write contract: read-only definitions can be replaced by any definition of the same value type, writable ones only by definitions that are written the same way, otherwise a `TypeError` is thrown.

const AtomKind = {
  primitive: 'primitive',
  primitiveFactory: 'primitive-factory',
  derived: 'derived',
  writableDerived: 'writable-derived'
} as const
type IAtomKind = (typeof AtomKind)[keyof typeof AtomKind]

blocks.text: `AtomKind` is a frozen constant object with no call parameters; `definition.kind` is always one of these four string literals and can drive `switch`/branching.
The four `kind`s form a discriminated union:

type IAtomDefinition<T> =

  | IPrimitiveFactoryDefinition<T>

The guard covers object and function thenables and reads `then` only once through the utils probe (`probeThenable` from `@migaia/utils/function`); a failing hostile getter is turned synchronously into a Store Keyed tagged `INVALID_OPTION`, with the original exception on `cause`. Factory definitions apply the same guard to the returned value on their first `get`/`peek`/`preview`.

rows: Every call produces a brand-new scope that never interferes with others.

The default (not the only) store for each `IRuntime`, cached in a `WeakMap<IRuntime, IAtomStore>`; a disposed old store is dropped and recreated. Meant for older instance-style APIs used without a Provider, so they share state on the same Runtime; Provider scenarios should each use their own `createAtomStore`.

Records a dependency edge inside the current Computed/Effect tracking window; outside a tracking context it is an ordinary read and does not throw. When the definition has no instance yet, one is created first according to its kind (a Signal or a Computed).
Untracked read that never records an edge. For "read once without becoming a dependency" (the `getSnapshot` of a React adapter is the typical case).

Speculative read for React concurrent rendering. When the definition already has a real instance in this store, it returns that instance's current value (`peek()` semantics); otherwise it computes a temporary value valid only for the current runtime version, creates no persistent instance, and drops the cached value after the Runtime's idle cleanup (a microtask by default) if it was never committed as a real instance. A `primitive-factory` must be marked `previewSafe` to run here, otherwise it throws; a cycle of self-dependency throws `[store] circular atom preview detected`.

blocks.code:
store.set(countDef, 1)
store.set(countDef, (previous) => previous + 1) // functional update
store.set(writableDerivedDef, ...customArgs) // goes through write(get, set, ...args)

blocks.text: `store.set(definition, ...args)` is wrapped in `runtime.batch(() => runtime.untracked(...))`: the batch makes all downstream recomputations caused by one `set` notify subscribers once, and `untracked` keeps the `set` itself from being recorded as a dependency by an outer Computed/Effect that is tracking.

items: When the target resolves to `primitive`/`primitive-factory`: it writes the underlying Signal's `.value`, accepting a value or a `(previous) => next` updater.

When the target resolves to `derived` (read-only): it throws `TypeError('[store] atom override resolved to a read-only definition')`. TypeScript normally prevents passing a read-only definition directly; this path is mostly hit when an override routes a writable definition to a read-only target.
When the target resolves to `writable-derived`: it calls `write(store.get, store.set, ...args)` and returns what `write` returns.

blocks.text: To write several source definitions at once, use `store.setMany`:

blocks.code:
store.setMany([
  [countDef, (previous) => previous + 1],
  [nameDef, 'Ada']
])

items: It accepts only source definitions (`atomDef`, `atomDefFactory`). If an override routes any entry to a non-source definition, it throws `OVERRIDE_CONTRACT`.

It first resolves every entry and runs every updater in order, and writes only after that. If any entry is rejected or any updater throws, every definition keeps its old value and no subscriber is notified.

When a definition appears more than once, a later entry's updater receives the value computed by the earlier one, the same result as calling `set` one by one. An updater that reads another definition sees the value from before the call.
The writes happen in one batch, so subscribers are notified once.

blocks.text: `store.sub(def, onChange)` subscribes to that one node through a reactive static observer instead of handing the underlying node to the caller, so the instantiation strategy (when to create a Signal/Computed, whether lazily) can evolve without breaking subscribers. The first run only records dependencies and does not call `onChange`; after that, every dependency change calls `onChange` inside `runtime.untracked()`. An exception thrown by `onChange` is caught and passed to `runtime.reportError(error, { phase: 'subscription-listener' })`, without stopping other subscribers or ending this subscription. The returned `unsubscribe` is idempotent and safe to call several times.

The three overloads correspond to three "the write contract must stay the same" rules (the reason is item 3 of section 10); breaking them throws `TypeError('[store] atom override must preserve the original write contract')`.
Behaviour details:

items: An override is a routing change, not node destruction: the underlying state of both the old and the new definition is kept in full. After switching, existing downstream of the old definition is forcibly invalidated (`invalidateResolved`: it only cuts downstream edges and does not dispose the node), and the next read resolves to the new target.

One definition can carry several stacked overrides (the latest call is on top, and resolution always takes the last layer); the undo function returned by `override()` removes only its own layer, whether or not it is currently on top.
Both override and undo clear the internal `preview` cache (`previews.clear()`), so `store.preview()` never reads a stale speculative value from before the override.
Resolution follows a possibly multi-layer override chain; a cycle throws `Error('[store] cyclic atom override')`.

After the store is disposed, calling `override()` throws `[store] cannot use a disposed atom store` at the entry; an undo function obtained earlier and called after disposal is a no-op (it does not throw).

rows: Whether the definition has an instance in this store with active subscribers; returns `false` when the definition was never `get`/`sub`bed, and the query itself creates no instance.

Removes only the instance of this one definition (cutting its edges and disposing the underlying node) without affecting other definitions in the store; returns whether anything was released. It tries both "the target after override resolution" and "the original definition passed in", covering instances created before an override took effect.
Number of definitions currently instantiated, usable as an observable assertion point for release behaviour.
Releases the whole scope; see section 9. Idempotent; repeated calls are no-ops.

sections.heading: 4.2 opticDef — writable projection with a custom lens

blocks.text: On write it first reads the current focus with `optic.get` and compares it with `Object.is` against the new value from the update function (or direct value); when equal it skips `set(source, ...)` and produces no empty write. `source` must be a "standard writable definition" (`set(update)` semantics), because `opticDef` calls `set(source, optic.set(currentSource, nextFocus))` under that contract.

sections.heading: 4.3 focusDef — built-in lens by field path

blocks.text: A built-in specialization of `opticDef`: reads walk the path with `Reflect.get`, writes shallow-copy each level along the path (`[...value]` for arrays, `{...value}` for objects) and write back, never mutating the original and needing no hand-written immutable update. The types support up to three levels; deeper nesting needs several `focusDef`s combined or an `opticDef`.
Boundary behaviour:

items: Calling it without any path segment throws `Error('[store] focusDef requires at least one path segment')`.
Reading through `null` or a non-object value midway throws `TypeError('[store] focusDef cannot read path segment <key>')`.
Writing through `null` or a non-object value midway (with more path left) throws `TypeError('[store] focusDef cannot write path segment <key>')`.
The write path handles the `__proto__` key specially, using `Object.defineProperty` instead of `Reflect.set` to avoid prototype pollution.

sections.heading: 4.4 splitDef — split an array by key

rows: Returns the writable item definition for the key; tokens are cached in an internal `Map`, so the same key always gives the same object reference, across stores too (this is the definition layer, not instances). Reads locate the index in the current source array with `keyOf`; if it is missing they throw `Error('[store] split def item was removed')`. Writes likewise throw `Error('[store] cannot write a removed split def item')`.

A `derivedDef` whose value is the frozen array of `of(key)` definitions for the current source items; compared with a custom `equals` (`shallowArrayEquals`: same length and `Object.is` item by item), so updates other than reorder/insert/delete do not rerun its downstream, and item identities stay stable while the order is unchanged.
Equivalent to `store.set(source, (previous) => spliceInsert(previous, item, index))`; `index` defaults to `+Infinity` (append) and is clamped to `[0, length]`.
Filters out every source element whose `keyOf` matches by SameValueZero and returns whether anything was removed.

Only clears `splitDef`'s own key → definition token cache, without releasing nodes already instantiated in the `AtomStore`; release those with `store.release(itemDef)` or `store.dispose()`. Returns the number of keys cleared.

blocks.text: A duplicate key in the source array (`keyOf` producing the same value twice) throws `Error('[store] splitDef keys must be unique')` when `items` is evaluated.

blocks.code:
class KeyedSplitCache<Key, Item> {
  get(key: Key): Item | undefined
  of(key: Key, create: () => Item): Item
  prune(
    isLive: (key: Key) => boolean,
    shouldEvict?: (item: Item) => boolean, // defaults to () => true
    onEvict?: (item: Item) => void
  ): number
  readonly size: number
  keys(): IterableIterator<Key>
  values(): IterableIterator<Item>
  clear(): void
}

blocks.text: The reusable keyed cache `splitDef` uses for `key → item definition` tokens. The constructor takes no parameters (internally an empty `Map`). `of(key, create)`: returns the cached value when it is truthy; when missing or falsy it calls `create()` and stores the result. `prune(isLive, shouldEvict?, onEvict?)`: for each cached `key`, an entry is evicted only when `isLive(key)` is `false` and `shouldEvict(item)` (default always `true`) is `true`, that is `!isLive(key) && shouldEvict(item)`; before eviction it calls `onEvict?.(item)` so the caller can release resources the item holds (for example dispose an instance); it returns the number of entries evicted. `splitDef(...).prune(store)` calls it with `isLive = (key) => activeKeysInSourceArray.has(key)` and no `shouldEvict`/`onEvict` (definition tokens hold nothing to dispose).

Source: `src/family/definition.ts`. An older "instance-style" family cached instances already bound to a Runtime, so a key was always the same state in every scope. The definition family splits that apart: a family caches only tokens, and the `AtomStore` a token lands in decides which scope holds its independent value.
`IFamilyKey = string | number | symbol`.

items: `familyDef(initial)` produces `atomDefFactory(() => initial(key), ...)` for each key, so a family definition's `kind` is always `'primitive-factory'` with `previewSafe: false`; to read family members in `store.preview()`, use `derivedFamilyDef` or accept that the preview path throws.
`derivedFamilyDef(read)` produces `derivedDef(read(key), ...)` for each key and is read-only.

Both return the cached token on each call; `family.size` is the number of strong cache entries; `family.forget(key)` explicitly breaks the canonical identity of that key (instances already created in an `AtomStore` are unaffected, but the next lookup of the same key returns a new token, so callers must stop using the old token, or one logical key splits into two unrelated states); `family.clear()` clears every entry.

blocks.text: Option validation: a non-object (`null` or not an `object`), or a failing read of `maxSize`/`debugLabel`, becomes a `RangeError` with `code: 'INVALID_OPTION'` and the message `[store] family maxSize must be a positive integer`; a non-string `debugLabel` throws `RangeError` with the message `[store] family debugLabel must be a string`; a `maxSize` that is not a positive safe integer also throws `RangeError`.

The strong cache is a `Map` reordered by access (`maxSize` entries). Beyond the limit it evicts the least recently accessed entry, but eviction only removes it from the strong cache and records it in a `Map<Key, WeakRef<Definition>>` (strong keys, weak values) as the canonical record. As long as the token is still strongly referenced elsewhere (for example instantiated in some `AtomStore`, or kept in a caller's variable), a later lookup of the same key finds the same token through `WeakRef.deref()` and promotes it back into the strong cache; only after the token is really garbage-collected does the same key create a new token. This relies on host support for `WeakRef` and `FinalizationRegistry`; without them, calling `familyDef(...)`/`derivedFamilyDef(...)` throws `Error('[store] family definitions require WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry; enable these capabilities in the host sandbox')` instead of silently degrading to "a new token every time".
`maxSize` must be a positive integer, otherwise `RangeError('[store] family maxSize must be a positive integer')` is thrown.

Source: `src/errors.ts`, `src/error-code.ts`, `src/error-text.ts`. Errors created by this module carry `source: 'store.keyed'` and a stable `code`; errors from Reactive or other module that already have a code keep their real owner. Failures of pure optic property access use `OPTIC_ACCESS_FAILED`: extensible native errors receive the code on the original object, keeping type, message and stack; frozen or non-Error primary values stay reachable through the cause of a coded fallback. Brand guards on arbitrary values return false when reading fails. Branch on source/code, not on the message.

The first three differ only in the runtime type they return (`Error`/`RangeError`/`TypeError`) and take the same arguments: `code` (required), `message` (required), `options?.cause` (optional, passed to the native `Error` constructor's `{ cause }`). Each result gets `source: 'store.keyed'` and `code` through `attachErrorIdentity` (from `@migaia/utils/error`), without touching `stack`/`name`. `createStoreKeyedAggregateError` also requires `errors: unknown[]` (which become `AggregateError.errors`) and takes no `cause` option.

Returns a getter bound to that runtime; before reading it checks `atom.runtime === runtime` and throws `Error('[store] cross-runtime atom access is not allowed')` otherwise.
Same, with the same cross-Runtime check before writing.

blocks.text: `AtomStore` keeps instances in an iterable `Map<definition, instance>` rather than a `WeakMap`: releasing has to walk them to cut edges and `dispose()` each underlying node, which a `WeakMap` cannot do. The smallest lifecycle unit is the whole store, not a single definition: the store strongly references every instance it created and releases them together on `store.dispose()`; to release one early, use `store.release(definition)`.

When the `init` of `atomDef(init)` is an object or array, the first instantiation in a store runs `cloneInitial` with `structuredClone`. A host without it throws `Error('[store] primitive initial values require structuredClone support')` (`code: 'ENV_UNSUPPORTED'`), and a value that cannot be structured-cloned (for example one containing functions) throws `Error('[store] primitive initial value cannot be cloned independently')` (`code: 'INVALID_OPTION'`, original exception on `cause`). There is deliberately no partial fallback, so prototypes are never silently changed and function fields never aliased. This guarantees the same definition never shares one mutable initial container across stores.

blocks.code: store.dispose()

blocks.text: 1. Immediately sets `disposed = true` (from then on every method entry throws `[store] cannot use a disposed atom store`) and clears the override table. 2. Calls every active subscription's unsubscribe (as returned by `sub()`) in turn; one failing unsubscribe does not stop the others, and errors are collected. 3. Releases every instance node through the internal `LifecycleScope` in reverse creation order (later derived nodes usually depend on earlier sources, and reverse order avoids a derived node reading released state while it disposes); one failing node is collected without stopping the rest. 4. With 0 collected errors it returns normally; with 1 it rethrows it as is; with several it throws them wrapped in `AggregateError('[store] atom store disposal failed')`.
`dispose()` is idempotent: repeated calls are no-ops and never throw again.

items: `store.release(def)`: removes one instance. It first tries the current override target and falls back to the original definition only when that released nothing, so even a definition overridden later can still have its pre-override instance removed correctly.
`store.dispose()`: removes the whole scope.

blocks.text: Cleaning the family/split key → token caches, such as `splitDef(...).prune(store)` and `familyDef(...).forget/clear`, never calls `store.release()`: the token caches and the store's instance table are two separate tables, each responsible for its own lifecycle.

`override()` and its undo function both call `previews.clear()`, so `store.preview()` never reads a speculative value matching the old routing at the moment an override switches. `preview()` short-circuits to `peek()` for definitions that already have a real instance; only definitions without one take the speculative path, and the value it produces is reused only within the current version clock value (read with `currentRuntimeVersion(runtime)` from `@migaia/reactive/extension`). After the Runtime's idle cleanup (a microtask by default) it is dropped if it never became a real instance, so a long-mounted Provider never keeps a speculative object forever because of one abandoned speculative render.

1. `store.get()` records dependency edges; `peek()`/`preview()` do not. `get()` records an edge only inside a tracking context (a Computed's `read`, an Effect callback); in plain synchronous code it behaves like `peek()`, but it is easier to misuse as "this will be tracked elsewhere too". Snapshot reads in React adapters (`getSnapshot`, `useSyncExternalStore`) must use `peek`/`preview`; using `get` would accidentally record the read in the dependency set of some other Computed outside the current render, causing hard-to-reproduce cross edges.

2. `store.set()` accepts only primitive / primitive-factory / writable-derived. Calling `set()` on a `derivedDef` throws `TypeError`. This is not only a TypeScript constraint: even if an `override()` routes a writable definition to a read-only one indirectly, the runtime throws when the write actually executes, so there is no "passes type checks, then the runtime lets it through" hole.

3. `override()` must keep the original write contract, which is the price of a uniform read side: `AtomStore.get()` reads all four `kind`s the same way, but `set()` needs to know which write semantics to apply to its arguments. If a primitive could be overridden by a custom `writable-derived`, the `update` argument passed to `set(def, update)` would mean completely different things under the two semantics (a new value or updater in the first, an arbitrary argument list for a custom `write` in the second), and the runtime could not tell which rules to apply. Read-only definitions have no such concern: they have no public write contract, so they can be routed to any definition of the same value type.

4. The `create()` of `atomDefFactory` may not run in `store.preview()` by default. React concurrent rendering may start a speculative render and then discard it entirely; if `create()` has side effects (opening a connection, writing a record into an external registry), a discarded render still makes the side effect happen, irreversibly. Factories that must run on the preview path must be declared with `previewSafeAtomDefFactory`, and are responsible for being pure, idempotent and free of externally observable side effects; this is the caller's promise, and the module does not verify it at run time.

5. `splitDef(...).prune(store)` only clears splitDef's own key → token cache and does not release the corresponding nodes already instantiated in the `AtomStore`. This is a deliberate split of responsibilities: `splitDef` knows which keys' definition tokens still matter, not whether an `AtomStore` has instantiated them. Release real instances with `store.release(itemDef)`, or rely on `store.dispose()` for the whole scope. When many keys roll through (for example a chat message list with constant inserts and deletes) and only `prune()` is called, `splitDef`'s internal cache does not leak, but old instances in the `AtomStore` keep accumulating.

6. The release unit is the whole store, not a single definition. This corrects an earlier design: an old comment claimed "instances can be reclaimed once a definition is no longer referenced" while an array strongly referenced every instance, so in practice nothing was ever reclaimed. The honest design now is that a store strongly references everything it created, `release(def)` is the only way to release one early, and batch reclamation happens only in `store.dispose()`.

7. `familyDef`/`derivedFamilyDef` need host support for `WeakRef` and `FinalizationRegistry`. Without them, calling the constructor throws an explanatory error at once instead of silently degrading to "a new token every time / never reclaim", which would produce a module that quietly slows down or leaks memory and is much harder to diagnose. A few embedded JavaScript engines or trimmed sandboxes may lack these globals; check the target runtime or add an equivalent polyfill.

8. Low-level optics functions such as `readOpticPath`/`writeOpticPath`/`KeyedSplitCache` are public exports, not private implementation. They are published through `@migaia/store-keyed/optics`, underpin `focusDef`/`splitDef`, and can be reused directly for custom optics or split logic (see section 11, complete example). They are pure primitives that do nothing related to `AtomStore` or dependency tracking: `readOpticPath`/`writeOpticPath` only read and write object paths, and `KeyedSplitCache` is only a keyed cache; none of them knows `IAtomDefinition`.
A combined example of "one state per session, independently subscribable fields, a list split by key, and test doubles":

Q: `store.set(def, value)` throws `TypeError: [store] atom override resolved to a read-only definition`. `def` (or the target it resolves to after an override) is a `derivedDef`. A read-only derivation has no write semantics; if the route goes through `override()`, check whether a step in the override chain points a writable definition at a read-only one.

Q: `store.override(a, b)` throws `TypeError: [store] atom override must preserve the original write contract`. The write semantics of `a` and `b` do not match: primitive/primitive-factory can only replace each other, and writable-derived can only be replaced by a writable-derived with the same Args/Result. Only read-only definitions are free of this restriction and can be routed to any definition of the same value type; see item 3 of section 10 for why.

Q: `familyDef(...)` throws `requires WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry` as soon as it is called. The target runtime lacks these two ES2021 globals (some trimmed mini-program or embedded JavaScript engines do). Check the host's support or add an equivalent polyfill; the error is never swallowed, because the module deliberately prefers failing loudly over silently degrading into never freeing memory.

Q: `store.preview(def)` throws `Error: [store] atom factory is not marked preview-safe`. `def` was created with `atomDefFactory` (`previewSafe: false`) and read on React's speculative render path (`preview()`). Either confirm the factory is pure and side-effect free and switch to `previewSafeAtomDefFactory`, or avoid reading it on the preview path.

Q: `splitDef(...).of(key)` throws `split def item was removed` / `cannot write a removed split def item`. The key is no longer in the source array (it may have been `remove()`d elsewhere, or the source array was replaced with `store.set()` without that item). Check with `todosSplit.items` or `store.get(todosSplit.source)` whether the key still exists before reading or writing; the token from `of(key)` is still the same object after the key disappears, but reads and writes keep failing until the key reappears in the source array.

Q: Why does `store.get(def)` after `store.dispose()` throw instead of returning the last value? A disposed store is in its end state, and every read or write entry first throws `[store] cannot use a disposed atom store`. This is intentional: a released scope must not keep being used silently, which would hide a caller bug of "forgot to open a new store". For new state, create a new one with `createAtomStore(runtime)`.

Q: After `familyDef(...).forget(key)`, can the old token still be used? Yes: the old token is still a valid definition, and `AtomStore` state already instantiated with it is unaffected. But after `forget`, looking up the same key creates a new token, and the old and new tokens are unrelated; if some code still holds the old token and keeps reading and writing with it, the logical key splits permanently into two states. After `forget`, make sure every caller switches to the new lookup result instead of mixing them.

Q: How do I create state grouped by key? Combine the public `familyDef`/`derivedFamilyDef` with `createAtomStore`. The unpublished instance-style family source and its tests have been deleted, and the `FAMILY_DISPOSED`/`EVICTION_FAILED` error codes that belonged only to that implementation were removed.

blocks.text: Cleanup of speculative values goes through the owning Runtime's idle channel (`scheduleIdle`, microtasks by default); no adapter-owned microtask queue is created.

Every split key lookup, uniqueness check, cache and deletion uses SameValueZero, as Map/Set do, so `-0` and `+0` are the same key and `NaN` equals itself. `shallowArrayEquals` still compares ordinary values item by item with `Object.is`. Store disposal clears the uncommitted preview cache, so even when a caller keeps a disposed store, that cache no longer holds speculative values. The family's canonical Map uses strong keys and weak values and is not a WeakMap; `forget` does not release existing store instances.

External usage is unknown; the root entry keeps no compatibility alias.

rows: 传入的不是 `atomDef`/`derivedDef`/... 产出的合法定义对象。
`atom override resolved to a read-only definition`
目标（可能经 override 解析后）是 `derived`，没有写语义。
`atom override must preserve the original write contract`
违反 第 3.4 节 的三条替换规则。
推测读之间出现循环依赖。
`focusDef requires at least one path segment`
`<label> cannot read path segment <key>` / `<label> cannot write path segment <key>`
路径中途遇到 `null`/非对象值。
读取时该 key 已不在源数组里。
`cannot write a removed split def item`
写入时该 key 已不在源数组里。
`keyOf` 对不同元素算出了相同的 key。
`family maxSize must be a positive integer`
`family definitions require WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry; enable these capabilities in the host sandbox`
宿主环境缺少这两个全局能力。
`<context> returned a thenable — async initial values are not supported here; compose with @migaia/resource instead (...)`
初值/工厂返回值是 thenable。
`atomDef({...})` 初值克隆失败（`structuredClone` 抛错）
`primitive initial value cannot be cloned independently`
值本身不可结构化克隆，原异常在 `cause`。
实例式 atom 的 `runtime` 与调用方绑定的 runtime 不一致。
释放多个实例/条目时不止一个抛错，原因各自保留在 `errors[]`。
`AtomStore` 内部所有权登记（继承自 `@migaia/reactive`）
`this node is already owned by another Runtime`
同一个 store 对象被 `claimOwnership` 到两个不同的 Runtime——正常使用路径下不会触发，出现即说明把同一个 store 错误地跨 Runtime 复用了。

cyclicOverride: Override routing contains a cycle and cannot resolve a final definition.

members.name: atomStoreDisposed
members.description: An atom store is used after disposal. * * Create a new store instead of reusing the disposed instance.

members.name: disposalFailed
members.description: Multiple entries fail to clean up while an atom store is disposed. An `AggregateError` exposes * each failure through `errors[]`. * * Treat this as a disposal failure and inspect each cause.

members.name: circularPreview
members.description: An atom preview cycle is detected within one render or preview stack. * * Check derived dependencies for cycles.

members.name: cyclicOverride
members.description: An atom override chain contains a cycle and cannot resolve its final definition. * * Check whether override targets point back to each other.

members.name: overrideContract
members.description: An override replaces a writable definition with a read-only target and breaks its write * contract. * * Preserve the read and write semantics across overrides.

members.name: previewUnsafe
members.description: A primitive factory without `previewSafe` is evaluated during preview. * * Mark the factory as `previewSafe` or avoid evaluating it during preview.

members.name: crossRuntime
members.description: An atom is accessed from a different `Runtime`, whose dependency graph cannot see the atom. * * Access the atom within its own `Runtime` instead of sharing it across runtimes.

members.name: envUnsupported
members.description: The host lacks `WeakRef`/`FinalizationRegistry` for the family cache or `structuredClone` for * independent primitive templates in AtomStore. * * Enable these capabilities in the host sandbox. This is a deployment issue.

members.name: opticAccessFailed
members.description: An application accessor or proxy fails while an optic reads or immutably copies its input. * Native mutable errors retain their identity and stack; frozen/non-Error originals stay on * cause. Inspect the application accessor rather than treating this as a missing path or target * key.

members.name: invalidOption
members.description: Input validation fails for `maxSize`, a non-atom definition, an empty or inaccessible focus * path, duplicate keys, a missing target key, or a thenable initial value. * * Correct the input named in the error message.

const StoreKeyedErrorCode = {
  atomStoreDisposed: 'ATOM_STORE_DISPOSED',
  disposalFailed: 'DISPOSAL_FAILED',
  circularPreview: 'CIRCULAR_PREVIEW',
  cyclicOverride: 'CYCLIC_OVERRIDE',
  overrideContract: 'OVERRIDE_CONTRACT',
  previewUnsafe: 'PREVIEW_UNSAFE',
  crossRuntime: 'CROSS_RUNTIME',
  envUnsupported: 'ENV_UNSUPPORTED',

rows: 传入的不是 `atomDef`/`derivedDef`/... 产出的合法定义对象。
`atom override resolved to a read-only definition`
目标（可能经 override 解析后）是 `derived`，没有写语义。
`atom override must preserve the original write contract`
违反 第 3.4 节 的三条替换规则。
推测读之间出现循环依赖。
`focusDef requires at least one path segment`
`<label> cannot read path segment <key>` / `<label> cannot write path segment <key>`
路径中途遇到 `null`/非对象值。
读取时该 key 已不在源数组里。
`cannot write a removed split def item`
写入时该 key 已不在源数组里。
`keyOf` 对不同元素算出了相同的 key。
`family maxSize must be a positive integer`
`family definitions require WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry; enable these capabilities in the host sandbox`
宿主环境缺少这两个全局能力。
`<context> returned a thenable — async initial values are not supported here; compose with @migaia/resource instead (...)`
初值/工厂返回值是 thenable。
`atomDef({...})` 初值克隆失败（`structuredClone` 抛错）
`primitive initial value cannot be cloned independently`
值本身不可结构化克隆，原异常在 `cause`。
实例式 atom 的 `runtime` 与调用方绑定的 runtime 不一致。
释放多个实例/条目时不止一个抛错，原因各自保留在 `errors[]`。
`AtomStore` 内部所有权登记（继承自 `@migaia/reactive`）
`this node is already owned by another Runtime`
同一个 store 对象被 `claimOwnership` 到两个不同的 Runtime——正常使用路径下不会触发，出现即说明把同一个 store 错误地跨 Runtime 复用了。

`<context> returned a thenable — async initial values are not supported here; compose with @migaia/resource instead (...)`
初值/工厂返回值是 thenable。
`atomDef({...})` 初值克隆失败（`structuredClone` 抛错）
`primitive initial value cannot be cloned independently`
值本身不可结构化克隆，原异常在 `cause`。
实例式 atom 的 `runtime` 与调用方绑定的 runtime 不一致。
释放多个实例/条目时不止一个抛错，原因各自保留在 `errors[]`。
`AtomStore` 内部所有权登记（继承自 `@migaia/reactive`）
`this node is already owned by another Runtime`
同一个 store 对象被 `claimOwnership` 到两个不同的 Runtime——正常使用路径下不会触发，出现即说明把同一个 store 错误地跨 Runtime 复用了。

symbols.name: createAtomStore
symbols.signature: export declare function createAtomStore(runtime: IRuntime): IAtomStore;
symbols.purpose: Creates a store: a scope that keeps its own value for every definition it reads. Definitions (`atomDef`, `derivedDef`, ...) hold no value, so the same definitions give separate values in each store, for example one store per server request or per test. A value is created the first time its definition is read and kept until `release(definition)` or `dispose()`.

runtime: IRuntime returned by @migaia/reactive createRuntime; it owns dependency graphs, batching, idle cleanup and error reporting.
Caller-owned IAtomStore; dispose it to release its subscriptions and instantiated graph nodes.

symbols.signature: export type IAtomStore = { readonly runtime: IRuntime; readonly disposed: boolean; get<T>(definition: IAtomDefinition<T>): T; /** * Reads without tracking, so an adapter snapshot does not create edges in another dependency * capture. */ peek<T>(definition: IAtomDefinition<T>): T; /** React/concurrent speculative read; value may be discarded after the turn. */ preview<T>(definition: IAtomDefinition<T>): T; /** * Writes a source definition with a new value or an updater of the previous value. Listed before * the general overload so the updater's `previous` parameter is typed from the definition. */ set<T>(definition: IPrimitiveDefinition<T> | IPrimitiveFactoryDefinition<T>, update: IAtomUpdate<T>): void; /** Writes any writable definition; a writable derived one returns its `write` result. */ set<T, Args extends readonly unknown[], Result>(definition: IWritableAtomDefinition<T, Args, Result>, ...args: Args): Result; /** * Writes source definitions within one batch and one untracked operation; subscribers are * notified once after the batch. The call first resolves every entry and runs every updater in * input order, then writes. An entry that resolves to a non-source definition (OVERRIDE_CONTRACT) * or an updater that throws leaves every atom unchanged. A repeated definition's updater receives * the value from its previous entry; updaters reading other atoms see the values from before the * call. * * Each entry keeps its own value type: `Ts` is inferred from the definitions only, so entries of * different types can share one call and each updater is checked against its own definition. */ setMany<Ts extends readonly unknown[]>(entries: { readonly [K in keyof Ts]: readonly [ IPrimitiveDefinition<Ts[K]> | IPrimitiveFactoryDefinition<Ts[K]>, IAtomUpdate<NoInfer<Ts[K]>> ]; }): void; /** * Subscribes to a definition and returns an unsubscribe function. * * Adapters subscribe through this boundary instead of accessing graph nodes, leaving * instantiation strategies independent. */ sub<T>(definition: IAtomDefinition<T>, onChange: () => void): IDisposer; /** Routes a read-only derived definition to any definition with the same value type. */ override<T>(definition: IDerivedDefinition<T>, replacement: IAtomDefinition<NoInfer<T>>): IDisposer; /** Replaces a primitive only with a definition that preserves standard `set(update)` semantics. */ override<T>(definition: IPrimitiveDefinition<T> | IPrimitiveFactoryDefinition<T>, replacement: IPrimitiveDefinition<NoInfer<T>> | IPrimitiveFactoryDefinition<NoInfer<T>>): IDisposer; /** Preserves the exact `Args` and `Result` contract of a writable derived definition. */ override<T, Args extends readonly unknown[], Result>(definition: IWritableDerivedDefinition<T, Args, Result>, replacement: IWritableDerivedDefinition<NoInfer<T>, NoInfer<Args>, NoInfer<Result>>): IDisposer; /** Reports whether this store has observers for the definition without exposing its graph node. */ isObserved<T>(definition: IAtomDefinition<T>): boolean; /** * Releases the instance for one definition. * * Unlike disposing the whole store, disposal of a legacy atom instance releases only its own * definition. Other definitions in the same store remain intact. */ release<T>(definition: IAtomDefinition<T>): boolean; /** Reports the number of instantiated definitions so release behavior is observable. */ readonly size: number; dispose(): void; };
symbols.purpose: A store returned by `createAtomStore` or `defaultAtomStore`: it keeps one value per definition, and its caller decides when to dispose it.
symbols.core:
runtime: The exact external IRuntime passed at store construction; it owns dependency tracking, batching and error reporting.
disposed: Terminal store flag set before disposal begins; subsequent state operations reject rather than recreating nodes.
size: Current number of instantiated definitions strongly retained by this store, excluding uncommitted preview entries.
get: Resolves active overrides, lazily materializes a definition and reads with Runtime dependency tracking.
get.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
Current scoped T; disposed stores use ATOM_STORE_DISPOSED and invalid definitions use INVALID_OPTION. Initialization/read failures preserve their owning semantics.
peek: Resolves and lazily materializes a definition but reads without creating a dependency edge in the current capture.
peek.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
Current untracked T with the same admission and initialization failures as get.
preview: Reads speculative state without permanently materializing uncommitted definitions. Existing instances are peeked; new factory values require previewSafe and cached previews expire through Runtime idle cleanup.
preview.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
Speculative T. Unsafe source creation uses PREVIEW_UNSAFE, preview cycles use CIRCULAR_PREVIEW; abandoned values need not become committed state.
set: Writes the resolved target inside Runtime batch/untracked. Primitive targets accept value or update(previous); writable-derived targets receive their exact args.
set.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
set.update: For a source definition (`atomDef`, `atomDefFactory`): the new value, or a function receiving the previous value and returning the next one. The function runs synchronously and its throw propagates.
set.args: Primitive: one value or synchronous previous-to-next callback, with throws propagated. Writable-derived: the Args declared by writableDef, forwarded unchanged.
Undefined for primitive writes or the writable callback Result. Writing a read-only target rejects with OVERRIDE_CONTRACT.
setMany: Writes several source definitions in one batch, so subscribers are notified once. Every entry is resolved and every updater runs before anything is written: if one entry is rejected or one updater throws, every definition keeps its old value.
setMany.entries: Pairs of a source definition (`atomDef`, `atomDefFactory`) and a new value or a function from the previous value to the next one. A definition listed twice gives its later updater the value computed by the earlier entry; an updater that reads another definition sees the value from before the call.
Undefined. An entry that an override routes to a non-source definition rejects the whole call with OVERRIDE_CONTRACT; an updater error propagates unchanged.
sub: Establishes dependency observation immediately without calling the listener initially. Later change callbacks run synchronously untracked; throws are reported to runtime.reportError and do not kill other subscriptions.
sub.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
sub.onChange: Caller synchronous no-argument notification; read the current snapshot with store.peek if needed. No result is used or awaited.
External IDisposer: a no-argument idempotent unsubscribe function. Store disposal also releases active subscriptions.
override: Adds one reversible read-routing layer while preserving write contracts. Read-only definitions accept same-value replacements; primitive targets require primitive/factory replacements; writable-derived targets preserve Args and Result.
override.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
override.replacement: Compatible definition token created by the same public constructors, with value and write types required by the corresponding overload.
Idempotent undo function; target state is retained. Incompatible contracts use OVERRIDE_CONTRACT and cyclic routes use CYCLIC_OVERRIDE, rolling back the attempted layer.
isObserved: Checks the resolved definition existing node observation state without creating an instance.
isObserved.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
True when an existing node is observed; false otherwise. Disposed stores and invalid definitions still reject.
release: Releases only one instantiated definition, first trying its override-resolved target and trying the original definition only if the first removes no instance. Other store instances remain intact.
release.definition: Definition token returned by atomDef, a derived/optic constructor or family lookup; the store owns its scoped instance.
True if an instance was removed and disposed, false when neither key had one. Disposal failures propagate.
dispose: Idempotently marks terminal and clears uncommitted preview values plus overrides, releases subscriptions, then drains instance ownership in reverse order. Retaining the disposed store does not retain values through its preview cache.
No result after cleanup attempts. One collected failure is thrown unchanged; multiple failures throw DISPOSAL_FAILED AggregateError with original errors reachable.

members.description: Writes source definitions within one batch and one untracked operation; subscribers are notified once after the batch. The call first resolves every entry and runs every updater in input order, then writes. An entry that resolves to a non-source definition (OVERRIDE_CONTRACT) or an updater that throws leaves every atom unchanged.
